claim_summary: Steward contributes a feedback-driven investing agent that coordinates typed specialist agents around code-assembled temporal memory, a deterministic trading-safety core, and outcome-graded, replay-verified prompt evolution.

claim_evidence.quote: We present Steward, a multi-agent LLM system in which nine agents trade a US equity portfolio through a brokerage API, in six sessions per trading day and with no human in the trading loop.

the system improves itself by governed self-evolution: code grades every decision against realised outcomes, a reflector proposes typed changes to the prompts, and a deterministic, reversible gate applies them but cannot reach an invariant core

process_validity.quote: across 1,632 calls validation failed on 13 sub-items, each isolated without losing a session.

temporal_validity.quote: Every decision was recorded before its outcome existed, so the live record is forward and free of the pre-training leakage that is hard to exclude in backtests of LLM agents [18].

task_performance.quote: held the Evening Analyst to account: its 38 directional next-day calls were right 37% of the time, below the 54% base rate of up days, and because the grade is computed by code (R2), this hit rate appeared in its own next-day prompt.

decision_utility.quote: Between June 22 and July 29 the semiconductor ETF fell 24.6%, QQQ 10.3% and SPY 2.0%, whereas the portfolio lost 0.3%, having exited its semiconductor positions in May on named triggers that are legible in the trace.

modules.name: Typed multi-agent portfolio decision pipeline
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the roles produce market ratings, portfolio targets and trade approvals. If the task family changed, the portfolio state, role schemas and action semantics would need redesign; although the inputs include time series, the module is not task-agnostic GTS.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-specific objective or validation criterion is embedded
R5:temporal function embedded in the task procedure

evidence.quote: Only the morning session may open positions: four analysts read the Web in parallel, a Portfolio Manager synthesises their typed reports with the shared memory of §4.2, and the plan passes through a deterministic order constructor, a blocking risk engine and an LLM Risk Manager before execution.
trend (price versus moving averages) → momentum (RSI, MACD) → volatility (Bollinger position, ATR) → volume (confirming or diverging) → support_resistance (levels, valuation flags).

modules.name: Code-assembled seven-layer memory and outcome grading
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the stored state and grades are portfolio positions, trading outcomes and next-day calls. A different task family would require redesigning these state fields and scoring targets; temporal ordering alone does not make this generic GTS memory.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-specific objective or validation criterion is embedded
R5:temporal function embedded in the task procedure

evidence.quote: They share a memory that code assembles from the system’s own record in seven layers, read by the Portfolio Manager every morning.

The evening session closes each trading day with two kinds of grading (R2). Code first assembles the evidence: the sells of the last two days and the buys of the last five with their realised returns, the last ten next-day calls scored against the next day’s return

What feeds forward is aggregated by code from that record: the calibration of L4, the hit rates of the next-day calls, missed themes that recur in at least two episodes or symbols over the last 14 evenings, and root causes that recur across at least two symbols.

modules.name: Governed quarterly prompt evolution
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the reflector consumes investing outcomes and proposes changes to trading-agent prompts, while the gate protects trading-specific agents and risk discipline. Changing task family would require redesigning the graded digest, target-agent schema and proposal semantics; the 90-day window is temporal, but the mechanism is not task-agnostic GTS.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-specific objective or validation criterion is embedded
R5:temporal function embedded in the task procedure

evidence.quote: Its input is a deterministic digest of 90 days of graded record (alpha against SPY, calibration by size, themes caught and missed, root causes of wrong trades and per-agent signal activity) together with every editable prompt, its current Learnings section and the previous quarter’s reflection.
The gate has two deterministic layers (Appendix C). The proposal schema rejects a malformed learning before it is staged, and a PromptEditor applies the rest under its own invariants.
A decision-replay harness passes recorded inputs through the prompt before and after a learning, with the rest of the input fixed, and compares the outputs structurally

modules.name: Invariant order-construction and risk core
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the core's order arithmetic, portfolio caps, stops and loss breaker enforce trading-specific objectives. Under a task-family change, the action space, temporal state and verifier would need redesign; the rules are not generic GTS validation.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-specific objective or validation criterion is embedded
R5:temporal function embedded in the task procedure

evidence.quote: skips an entry more than 5% from the market price, and skips a trade whose risk/reward falls below 1.2 once execution has moved its prices. Risk/reward is a computed field that the Risk Manager audits against a floor of 1.5.
A blocking engine rejects BUYs that would drive cash negative, positions above 20% of equity, sectors above 40%, net exposure above 90%, entries without a stop, and any buy after a 3% daily loss.

notes: Outcome grading writes into persistent memory, so the memory and short-term feedback mechanisms are closely coupled.
